title: Enabling HPC Scientific Workflows for Serverless
problem: Workflow management systems struggle to orchestrate complex computational tasks that combine edge computing, big data analytics, and AI with traditional scientific calculations in HPC environments. It is difficult to identify patterns within the growing population of diverse HPC workflows.
motivation: Serverless computing offers dynamic resource allocation, quick response time, fine-grained resource management, and auto-scaling capabilities that could improve efficiency and reduce costs of HPC workflow execution.
method: The framework integrates a traditional HPC workflow generator with an HPC serverless workflow management system to create diverse benchmark suites of scientific workflows. Workflows are executed on different serverless platforms and compared against execution on traditional local containers using comprehensive performance evaluation.
key_novelty: First framework bridging traditional HPC workflow management with serverless computing paradigms, demonstrating that serverless platforms can efficiently execute complex scientific workflows.
contributions: Framework integrating HPC workflow generators with serverless workflow management systems
Benchmark suites of scientific workflows with diverse characteristics for serverless platforms
Comprehensive empirical comparison of container-based versus serverless workflow execution
Demonstration that serverless reduces CPU usage by 78.11% and memory usage by 73.92% without performance degradation
